spots.name: California State Capitol

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The California State Capitol is the seat of the California state government, located in Sacramento, the state capital of California. The building houses the chambers of the California State Legislature, made up of the assembly and the senate, along with the office of the governor of California.

spots.name: Sacramento Valley Station
spots.summary: Sacramento Valley Station is an Amtrak railway station in the city of Sacramento, California, at 401 I Street on the corner of Fifth Street, built in 1926 on the site of China Slough. It is the thirteenth busiest Amtrak station in the country, and the second busiest in the Western United States.

spots.name: Tower Bridge

spots.name: Sutter's Fort

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Sutter's Fort was a 19th-century agricultural and trade colony in the Mexican Alta California province. Established in 1839, the site of the fort was originally part of a utopian colonial project called New Helvetia by its builder John Sutter, though construction of the fort proper would not begin until 1841.

spots.name: California State Railroad Museum
spots.summary: The California State Railroad Museum is a museum in the California State Parks system that interprets the role of railroads in the Western U.S. It is located in Old Sacramento State Historic Park at 111 I Street, Sacramento, California.

spots.name: Leland Stanford Mansion
spots.summary: The Leland Stanford Mansion, often known simply as the Stanford Mansion, is a historic mansion and California State Park in Sacramento, California, which serves as the official reception center for the Government of California and one of the official workplaces of the governor of California.

spots.name: Crocker Art Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: The Crocker Art Museum is the oldest art museum in the Western United States, located in Sacramento, California. Founded in 1885, the museum holds one of the premier collections of Californian art.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral of the Blessed Sacrament is the Catholic cathedral of the Diocese of Sacramento in Sacramento, California, United States. It is the seat of Bishop Jaime Soto. The cathedral is located downtown Sacramento at the intersection of 11th and K Streets.

spots.name: Old Sacramento State Historic Park
spots.summary: Old Sacramento State Historic Park occupies around one third of the property within the Old Sacramento Historic District of Sacramento, California. The Old Sacramento Historic District is a U.S. National Historic Landmark District.

spots.name: Delta King
spots.summary: Delta King is a 285-foot-long sternwheel steamboat (87 m) and the sister ship of Delta Queen, built in Glasgow, Scotland and Stockton, California for the California Transportation Company's service between Sacramento and San Francisco, California. She entered service in 1927 and continued until 1940.

spots.name: Cesar Chavez Plaza
spots.summary: Cesar Chavez Plaza, or Cesar Chavez Park, is a city park in Sacramento, California, named after César Chávez. For more than a century the downtown square has been a focal point for community activities, including the Farmers' Market, music concerts, and community rallies.

spots.name: California State Capitol Museum

spots.summary: The California State Capitol Museum consists of a museum in and grounds around the California State Capitol in Sacramento, California, United States. The building has been the home of the California State Legislature since 1869.

spots.name: California State Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The California State Library is the state library of the U.S. state of California. It was founded in 1850 by the California State Legislature. The library collects, preserves, generates and disseminates a wide array of information.

spots.name: The California Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The California Museum is the state history museum of the US state of California, located in its capital city of Sacramento. The museum is housed within the March Fong Eu Secretary of State Building complex at 1020 O Street, one block from the California State Capitol.

spots.name: Sacramento History Museum
spots.summary: The Sacramento History Museum is a historical museum in Sacramento, California, which interprets the history of Sacramento and the California Gold Rush. The museum is located within the Old Sacramento State Historic Park, situated along the Sacramento River between the Tower Bridge and I Street Bridge.

spots.name: Westminster Presbyterian Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Westminster Presbyterian Church, located at 13th St. and N Street in Sacramento, California, was built in 1927. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2003.

spots.name: I Street Bridge
spots.summary: The I Street Bridge is a historic metal truss double-deck swing bridge that crosses the Sacramento River to link the capital city of Sacramento, California, with Yolo County to the west.

spots.name: Big Four House
spots.summary: The Big Four Building is a historic 19th-century building in Downtown Sacramento, California. It is now located within Old Sacramento State Historic Park and the Old Sacramento National Historic District.

names.ja: ビッグ・フォー・ハウス

spots.name: Pony Express Terminal
spots.summary: The Pony Express Terminal, also known as the B. F. Hastings Bank Building, is a historic commercial building at 1000 2nd Street in Sacramento, California. Built in 1852, it was the western endpoint of the Pony Express from 1860 to 1861, the period of the service's operation.

spots.name: Sacramento Masonic Temple
spots.summary: The Sacramento Masonic Temple, built between 1913 and 1918, is a five-story building on J Street in downtown Sacramento, California. The building was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2001.

spots.name: Esquire Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Esquire Tower, also known as Esquire Plaza, is a 322-foot 248,816 square foot office building in downtown Sacramento, California. The Esquire IMAX Theater as well as a restaurant are located on the ground level of Esquire Plaza.

spots.name: Heilbron House
spots.summary: The Heilbron House is a historic mansion in Downtown Sacramento, California. Built in 1881, it was initially the home of August Heilbron, a cattle rancher, merchant, and landowner who came from Germany.

spots.name: Renaissance Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Renaissance Tower is a 113 m (371 ft) skyscraper in Sacramento, California, completed in 1989. The 28 story tower was the tallest in the city when completed, and is now the fifth.

spots.name: Park Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Park Tower is a 380-foot (120 m) skyscraper in Sacramento, California, completed in 1991. The 26-story tower was the tallest in the city when completed. The building was named U.S. Bank Plaza until U.S. Bank moved to U.S. Bank Tower in 2008.

spots.name: What Cheer House
spots.summary: What Cheer House, also at times called the Sackett Hotel and Grand Hotel, is a historical building in Sacramento, California. What Cheer House is a California Historical Landmark No. 597 listed on May 22, 1957. The What Cheer House was first used as hotel, the Sackett Hotel.

spots.name: Robert T. Matsui United States Courthouse

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Robert T. Matsui United States Courthouse is a courthouse in Sacramento, California. It is home to the Sacramento Division of the United States District Court for the Eastern District of California. It is located at 500 I Street and is named for the late congressman Bob Matsui.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Robert T. Matsui United States Courthouse

spots.name: Eagle Theatre
spots.summary: The Eagle Theatre in Gold Rush-era Sacramento was the first permanent theatre to be built in the state of California. Established in 1849 this relatively small structure was originally wood-framed and canvas-covered with a tin roof and a packed earth floor. The theatre was flooded on Jan 4, 1850.

spots.name: Statue of Thomas Starr King
spots.summary: A statue of the American minister Thomas Starr King by Haig Patigian stands in Sacramento, California, in the grounds of the California State Capitol.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Statue of Thomas Starr King (Sacramento, California)

spots.name: Statue of Junípero Serra
spots.summary: A statue of Junípero Serra in Capitol Park, near the California State Capitol, in Sacramento, California, was installed from 1967 until 2020. The statue was put in storage after demonstrators toppled it during a racial justice protest.

spots.name: Sacramento City Library

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: The Sacramento City Library, also known as Central Branch, is part of the Sacramento Public Library system, and faces I Street in Sacramento, California near Sacramento City Hall.

spots.name: Sacramento State University Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Sacramento State University Library is the central library for the campus of California State University, Sacramento. With over 1.4 million volumes, it is the third largest library in the California State University. It is part of the California State Depository Library Program.

spots.name: Sacramento Convention Center Complex
spots.summary: The Sacramento Convention Center Complex is a complex of entertainment venues and a convention center located in downtown Sacramento, California. The complex consists of the SAFE Credit Union Performing Arts Center, the Sacramento Memorial Auditorium, and the Jean Runyon Little Theater.

Several different combinations are offered, and the staff is also happy to build your pizza to order. The vegetarian pesto pizza, with sundried tomato and feta cheese, is especially good. spots.name: Tower Cafe

spots.summary: A great breakfast spot, busy at any time of day. There's sometimes a line, but absolutely worth it. It serves breakfast, lunch and dinner daily. Breakfast served 8-11AM, Monday through Friday. Brunch served 8AM-2PM, Saturday and Sunday. Voted Best Breakfast and Best Sunday Brunch in the 2009 Sacramento magazine readers poll. spots.name: Pine Cove Tavern

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Classic dive, possibly the best in Sacramento. Has gotten massively popular on weekends, but manages not to become unpleasant or lose its "divey" feel. Decently priced. Darts and pitchers make for a laid-back time. Avoid the popcorn machine; rumors abound about its level of sanitation. Karaoke two nights a week draws quite a crowd.

spots.name: Ella Dining Room & Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Ella serves its fabulous food, family-style and encourages diners to share. Their great bar serves fantastic concoctions like home made gin and tonics and "limeade," making for a perfect place for friends and family alike. The fabulous interior was created by award winning design firm, UXUS.

spots.name: Streets Pub and Grub

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Trendy "upscale dive" right in the heart of Sac's midtown nightlife. Not really big enough to compensate for its popularity anymore. Drinks are average range. Quieter with a more laid-back vibe on weeknights. Worth a stop, but not exactly an institution.

spots.name: Faces

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Faces is a popular gay-friendly club. Pricey cover, but the good strong drinks can quickly make up the difference. Faces has now doubled in size with an upstairs and a pool in the back. Plays R&B on video floor and House on other dance floor.

spots.summary: A modern-day diner with a retro feel, Jack's grills and roasts meats for sandwiches and salads and offers comfort food side dishes like mashed potatoes, mac & cheese, and garlic fries. Additional locations in the greater metropolitan area.

spots.name: Benny's

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Casual and often-crowded dive not far from midtown. Large back area provides extra room. On busy nights, a bartender will operate in back as well. Great place for drinks, and the Mexican food next door is a popular after-the-bar stopoff.

spots.summary: A basement bar in Old Sacramento that is a relic of a different era. Black ceilings, medieval chandeliers, and strong drinks make this dive bar worth visiting in Old Sacramento.

spots.summary: Quintessential Sacramento taqueria known for tacos, burritos, mulitas and more. Multiple locations in the region. An absolute must-try if looking for Mexican food in town.
